newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy minister Di Pietro under new investigation.
newsitem.headline: Italy minister Di Pietro under new investigation.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Thursday he had confidence in his Public Works minister Antonio Di Pietro despite newspaper reports that the former graft-busting magistrate was under investigation for corruption.

The newspapers reported that magistrates in the north Italian city of Brescia were conducting a preliminary investigation and that a number of unspecified corruption allegations were being weighed up.
Prodi who brought Di Pietro into his cabinet after riding to victory at the head of a centre-left coalition in April elections was quick to stand by his minister.
"I confirm full confidence in minister Di Pietro and in the magistracy," Prodi was quoted as saying by a spokesman.
Di Pietro, as a member of an elite group of magistrates in Milan which swept out the old governing class on a tide of corruption, spearheaded the "clean hands" anti-graft crusade.
"Antonio Di Pietro is again under investigation by the Public Prosecutor's office of Brescia," said Milan daily Corriere della Sera.
"The possible charges, which refer to various episodes, are several and for the time being are top secret," the newspaper added.
One of the most popular public figures in the country, Di Pietro resigned abruptly from the magistracy in December 1994 in circumstances which have never been fully explained.
He was the target of an earlier probe by Brescia magistrates into allegations of corruption and of profiting from holding a public office. But all charges against him were dropped in April.
Magistrates were also now investigating fresh allegations of irregularities in the way Di Pietro conducted investigations while he himself was a magistrate, newspapers reported.
